value.title: Grok/xAI provider wiring
value.description: Add Grok/xAI as the EXISTING openai-compat provider pointed at https://api.x.ai/v1, mirroring the DeepSeek wiring at its three resolution sites, plus a single shared isXaiEndpoint() predicate. NO new ProviderName value, NO new adapter class. Touch-points: (1) src/orchestrator/model-resolver.ts SHORTHAND_MAP — add grok shorthands {provider:'openai-compat', modelId} and make the openai-compat endpoint-attach branch select https://api.x.ai/v1 for grok* (vs https://api.deepseek.com for deepseek*); (2) src/providers/factory.ts validateApiKey openai-compat case — add an isXaiEndpoint(endpoint) arm requiring apiKey ?? process.env.XAI_API_KEY and throwing a clear 'configured to use Grok/xAI but XAI_API_KEY is not set' error; (3) src/providers/factory.ts createClient openai-compat case key-injection — add a parallel isXaiEndpoint arm injecting XAI_API_KEY (the OpenAICompatAdapter constructor call is UNCHANGED). Add isXaiEndpoint(endpoint?:string):boolean as the SOLE place the 'api.x.ai' host string is matched, reused by both factory sites (mirror however DeepSeek's host is matched today). src/fleet/index.ts validateManifestCredentials already calls validateApiKey(provider, role, apiKey, endpoint) per child section, so adding the xAI arm makes the fleet pre-spawn credential check recognize Grok with ZERO edits to index.ts. This sprint changes NO fleet behavior and NO tier logic (that is Sprint 2).

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build) and zero typecheck errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).

The full test suite passes with zero new failures (npm run test); the 6 pre-existing tests/e2e/cockpit-integration.test.ts MCP 'Connection closed' failures are the only allowed failures and are confirmed unrelated.

resolveProviderModel('grok') and the other added grok shorthands return { provider:'openai-compat', modelId:<the grok model id>, endpoint:'https://api.x.ai/v1' }, exactly mirroring the deepseek shorthand shape; a collocated test asserts the provider, modelId, and endpoint.

validateApiKey('openai-compat', role, undefined, 'https://api.x.ai/v1') THROWS a message naming Grok/xAI and XAI_API_KEY when neither providerConfig.apiKey nor process.env.XAI_API_KEY is set, and does NOT throw when XAI_API_KEY is present; the existing api.deepseek.com and no-key (Ollama) behaviors are unchanged.

createClient for an openai-compat provider at an api.x.ai endpoint injects XAI_API_KEY into the OpenAICompatAdapter (parallel to the DEEPSEEK_API_KEY arm), verified by a test that asserts the adapter is constructed with the xAI key (and that Ollama/other openai-compat endpoints keep the no-key behavior).

isXaiEndpoint(endpoint) is the ONLY place 'api.x.ai' is matched; a grep/test confirms 'api.x.ai' appears solely inside isXaiEndpoint, and both validateApiKey and createClient call it. ProviderName is unchanged (still anthropic|openai|google|openai-compat|claude-code).
lint passes (npm run lint, zero errors); no new disallowed imports; the change is confined to model-resolver.ts + factory.ts (+ their tests).

nonGoals: Do NOT add a new ProviderName value or a GrokAdapter class — Grok is openai-compat.
Do NOT add tier logic, FleetChild.tier, or any buildChildConfig change (Sprint 2).
Do NOT edit validateManifestCredentials' loop body — the xAI arm in validateApiKey must make it work for free.
Do NOT change the DeepSeek or Ollama openai-compat behavior.
Do NOT hardcode an XAI_API_KEY or commit any secret.
stopConditions: grok* resolves to openai-compat @ api.x.ai/v1, XAI_API_KEY is validated+injected only via the single isXaiEndpoint predicate, ProviderName unchanged, and build/typecheck/test/lint green with no new failures

Collocated tests cover shorthand resolution, key-required/throw, key-injection, the single-predicate invariant, and DeepSeek/Ollama non-regression. Build/typecheck/test/lint green.

value.title: TierProviderPolicy + buildChildConfig tier overlay
value.description: Add a closed difficulty-tier enum on FleetChild and a TierProviderPolicy that maps each tier to a planner/generator/evaluator provider block, overlaid in buildChildConfig BEFORE the existing shallow-merge so the result is byte-identical when tier is absent. New file src/fleet/tier-policy.ts exports: type RoleProviderBlock = {provider: ProviderName; model: string; endpoint?: string|null}; type TieredRoleBlock = {planner: RoleProviderBlock; generator: RoleProviderBlock; evaluator: RoleProviderBlock}; type DifficultyTier = 'default'|'cheap'|'standard'|'hard'|'frontier'; a TIER_POLICY table (cheap->DeepSeek openai-compat api.deepseek.com, standard->Grok openai-compat api.x.ai/v1, hard->Anthropic Sonnet, frontier->Anthropic Opus); resolveTier(tier): TieredRoleBlock|undefined ('default'/undefined -> undefined = NO overlay); knownTiers(). claude-code is NEVER in the table (children build = TOOL_ROLES). src/fleet/manifest.ts FleetChildSchema gains `tier: z.enum(['default','cheap','standard','hard','frontier']).optional()`. src/fleet/child-config.ts buildChildConfig adds an applyTier(base, child.tier) step that, when resolveTier returns a block, sets base.planner/generator/evaluator = {...base.role, ...block.role} — applied BEFORE the UNCHANGED `const merged = {...base, ...(child.config ?? {})}` at child-config.ts:43 so an explicit child.config still wins. When tier is undefined or 'default', applyTier returns base UNCHANGED and the whole function output is byte-identical to today.

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build) and zero typecheck errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
The full test suite passes with zero new failures (npm run test); only the 6 known cockpit-integration MCP failures may fail; the existing fleet child-config/manifest tests pass unchanged.

FleetChildSchema parses a child WITH tier (any enum value) and WITHOUT tier; a tier outside the closed enum is a ZodError; a manifest with no tier on any child parses field-for-field identically to before (the new field is optional and absent).

TierProviderPolicy.resolveTier returns undefined for 'default' and undefined input, and the correct TieredRoleBlock for cheap (DeepSeek), standard (Grok openai-compat https://api.x.ai/v1), hard (anthropic Sonnet), frontier (anthropic Opus). No tier block places claude-code on any role.

buildChildConfig(child) with NO tier returns a BoberConfig deep-equal to the pre-change DeepSeek-default output — proven by a test that constructs the expected config (planner/generator/evaluator on DeepSeek) and asserts deepEqual. This is the byte-identical guarantee.

buildChildConfig(child) with tier='standard' yields planner/generator/evaluator on provider 'openai-compat' with endpoint 'https://api.x.ai/v1'; tier='hard' yields provider 'anthropic' + a Sonnet model; tier='frontier' yields 'anthropic' + an Opus model; tier='cheap' yields DeepSeek. Each asserted on the parsed BoberConfig.

child.config precedence is preserved: a child with BOTH tier='standard' AND child.config.generator={provider:'anthropic',model:'...'} yields generator on anthropic (child.config wins over the tier block), proving the overlay runs BEFORE the shallow-merge at child-config.ts:43.
lint passes (npm run lint, zero errors); the change is confined to tier-policy.ts (new), manifest.ts, child-config.ts (+ tests); no new SDK/network imports; ProviderName unchanged.

nonGoals: Do NOT place claude-code in any tier block (children build = tool roles).
Do NOT add the ToolRoleGuard (Sprint 3) — though tier blocks must never produce a claude-code tool role in the first place.
Do NOT change the decomposer EXPAND prompt or the never-throw validateManifest shape guard.
Do NOT add BoberConfig.fleet / blackboard / Phase B fields.
Do NOT alter the `merged = {...base, ...(child.config ?? {})}` line itself (apply the overlay BEFORE it).
stopConditions: A tier-less child config is deep-equal to today's DeepSeek default, each tier maps to its specified provider block, child.config still wins, and build/typecheck/test/lint are green with no new failures

value.title: ToolRoleGuard (build-time, fail-fast)
value.description: Reject at manifest-build time any child whose RESOLVED BoberConfig would place the claude-code provider on a TOOL_ROLE (curator/generator/evaluator/codeReview), throwing BEFORE any child is spawned. Add a new EXPORTED predicate isToolRole(role: RoleName): boolean to src/config/role-providers.ts derived from the authoritative TOOL_ROLES constant (role-providers.ts:25), and export the existing effectiveProvider. New file src/fleet/tool-role-guard.ts exports: type ToolRoleViolation = {childFolder: string; role: RoleName; provider: 'claude-code'}; check(child: FleetChild, resolved: BoberConfig): ToolRoleViolation|null (pure, never throws — for each TOOL_ROLE, if effectiveProvider(role, resolved)==='claude-code' return the violation); assertManifest(manifest: FleetManifest): void which builds each child config via buildChildConfig and THROWS a named Error identifying child.folder+role on the first violation. Wire assertManifest into the fail-fast credential phase in src/fleet/index.ts — call it alongside/just before validateManifestCredentials (BOTH run before coordinator.execute), so no child is spawned when it throws. The never-throw validateManifest is UNCHANGED; the guard is a separate throwing call. The no-flag fleet path stays byte-identical (a clean manifest passes with no throw, no side effects).

successCriteria.description: The project builds with zero TypeScript errors (npm run build) and zero typecheck errors in strict mode (npm run typecheck).
The full test suite passes with zero new failures (npm run test); only the 6 known cockpit-integration MCP failures may fail; existing fleet index/role-providers tests pass unchanged.

Exported isToolRole(role) returns true for 'curator','generator','evaluator','codeReview' and false for 'planner','researcher','chat', and is derived from the authoritative TOOL_ROLES (a test asserts isToolRole agrees with TOOL_ROLES membership — no independently re-declared literal).

ToolRoleGuard.check(child, resolved) returns a ToolRoleViolation {childFolder, role, provider:'claude-code'} when claude-code resolves onto a tool role (e.g. child.config.generator.provider='claude-code'), and returns null for a clean config; check never throws.

ToolRoleGuard.assertManifest(manifest) THROWS a named error whose message contains the offending child.folder and role when any child would place claude-code on a tool role, and does NOT throw for a clean manifest (including one whose children carry tiers from Sprint 2).

assertManifest runs in the fail-fast phase BEFORE coordinator.execute in runFleet (src/fleet/index.ts): a test drives the fleet path (or runFleet with injected deps) with a claude-code-on-generator manifest and asserts it throws and that the coordinator/spawn was never invoked.

The never-throw validateManifest is unchanged and the no-flag fleet path is byte-identical: a clean tier-less manifest passes assertManifest with no throw, and the existing fleet behavior (and ~203-test suite) is unaffected.
lint passes (npm run lint, zero errors); change confined to role-providers.ts (new export), tool-role-guard.ts (new), index.ts (wire the call) + tests; no new SDK/network imports.

nonGoals: Do NOT modify the never-throw validateManifest (the guard is a separate throwing call).
Do NOT re-declare the tool-role list — isToolRole must derive from the authoritative TOOL_ROLES.

Do NOT change tier mapping (Sprint 2) or Grok wiring (Sprint 1).
Do NOT spawn or run children to test the guard — it is a pure pre-spawn check.
